findings: FY25 covers the 52 weeks to 1 February 2025; FY24 comparatives are restated on a 52-week basis to 27 January 2024 (statutory FY24 was 53 weeks to 3 February 2024) — source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/JD.L/20260904T195955Z/sources/filings/bodies/e544e58eca35fb32.txt
Group revenue £11,458m (+10.2% reported; +12.0% constant currency); organic sales growth 5.8% (LFL +0.3%, new space/conversions +5.5%), vs estimated market growth 3.8% — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt
Gross margin before adjusting items 47.8% (FY24 48.0%, −20bps); excluding Hibbett and Courir, margin flat at 48.0% — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt

Operating profit before adjusting items after interest on lease liabilities £937m (FY24 £940m, −0.3%; +0.8% CC); operating margin 8.2% vs 9.0% (−80bps reported, −90bps CC) — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt

Profit before tax and adjusting items £923m (FY24 £961m, −4.0%; −2.9% CC), in line with January guidance; reduction driven partly by £35m higher net finance expense ex lease interest from lower cash and acquisition borrowings — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt
Statutory PBT £715m (FY24 £811m, −11.8%); statutory operating profit £903m (FY24 £927m); statutory net finance expense £188m (FY24 £116m) — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt
Adjusted basic EPS 12.39p (FY24 12.81p, −3.3%); statutory basic EPS 9.50p (FY24 10.45p, −9.1%) — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt

Geographic revenue mix FY25: North America £4,242m (37%, +27% incl. six months Hibbett), Europe £3,510m (31%, +9.5% incl. two months Courir), UK £3,205m (28%, −4.1% mainly non-core divestments), Asia Pacific £501m (4%, +0.4%) — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt
Germany called out as challenging vs southern Europe success: structurally higher people costs and lower consumer appetite for sports fashion — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt

Channel mix: stores £9,081m (+15.7%, 79% of revenue); online £2,251m (−2.9%, 20%); online −6.6% ex acquisitions; shift reflects post-Covid store recovery, store investment and online profitability focus — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt
Operating cashflow net of lease repayments £1,245m (FY24 £1,161m, +7.2%); lease liability repayments £420m — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt
Cash and cash equivalents £695m at period end; net cash before lease liabilities £52m (FY24 £1,032m); interest-bearing loans and borrowings £679m (FY24 £130m) — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt

Hibbett acquisition funded via $1bn term loan drawn 25 July 2024; $700m outstanding at 1 Feb 2025 after post-acquisition repayments; Group refinancing £700m RCF, $300m asset-backed loan and $700m Hibbett term loan, expected H1 FY26 — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt

Capital expenditure £515m (stores & gyms £346m, supply chain £110m, technology & other £59m); medium-term guidance capex to trend from c.5% of revenue to 3–3.5%, with ~70% directed to North America and Europe — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt

Total dividend per share proposed 1.00p (FY24 0.90p, +11.1%); final dividend 0.67p proposed; FY25 equity dividends paid £48m; post-period £100m share buyback commenced 9 April 2025 — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt

Adjusting items net charge £208m (FY24 £155m): Derby DC closure impairment £76m (closed Sep 2024); European store estate review — 46 stores to close, £29m impairment; acquisition costs Hibbett/Courir £45m; amortisation of acquired intangibles £57m; Genesis/DTLR put-call revaluation £62m; Applied Nutrition disposal gain £78m — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt

Genesis Topco (North America holding company): Group owns 80%, 20% NCI remains; March 2025 amendment defers exercise to two equal 10% instalments post-FY2029 and post-FY2030 (was four 5% instalments); option price EBITDA-based; total liability cap unchanged at £1.5bn — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt

Hibbett: acquired 25 Jul 2024 for $1,077m (1,179 stores); expected earnings accretive first full year; cost synergies at least $25m medium term; US integration one-off cash cost ~1× annual savings — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt
Courir: acquired 27 Nov 2024 for €391m (306 stores); €198m acquired bank debt repaid; EC remedies required sale of 21 stores across France and Portugal before FY25 end — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt

People/infrastructure flags: >£100m additional people cost over last two years (wage inflation, age-banding removal); Heerlen DC delayed ~1 year with increased costs, now back on track (automated store orders FY26 peak, online FY27); ~£60m spent securing IT infrastructure/back-office resilience — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt

Updated medium-term plan (April 2025): organic revenue ahead of market estimated 2–3% p.a.; space growth contribution to settle ~3–4%; profit growth ahead of revenue beyond FY26; focus on profitability, cash generation and shareholder returns — source: e544e58eca35fb32.txt
